study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Jalbrzikowski et al., Am J Psychiatry, 2019
study_identification_part.si4_title: Age-Associated Deviations of Amygdala Functional Connectivity in Youths With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders: Relevance to Psychotic Symptoms

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: The authors created normative growth charts of amygdala functional connectivity in typically developing youths, assessed age-associated deviations of these trajectories in youths with psychosis spectrum disorders, and explored how these disruptions are related to clinical symptomatology.
study_characteristics_part.sc3_study_design_other: Mixed: One longitudinal data set and three cross-sectional data sets were combined.

nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper creates a new model and primarily focuses on validating it by applying it to clinical groups and showing consistency across sites. There is no explicit mention of validation on the training data itself or using non-independent resampling methods (e.g., bootstrap, k-fold cross-validation) to assess generalizability within the typically developing cohort.

nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The normative model was constructed using all available typically developing data. There is no indication of a train/test split or k-fold cross-validation where normative parameters were re-estimated on independent subsets of the *same domain* (i.e., within the combined healthy control data).
nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: Here, we extend these /uniFB01 ndings by combining different developmental data sources to form a large data set and construct a normative template of age-related changes to be used as a growth chart for the development of amygdala connectivity.
